decisions.evidence: The filename and authoritative character list identify proper-name Wrecker; a wrecker changes it to a generic noun.
Every revision fails to name Wraith in the dead ping; Great/Greg are phonetic errors.
The filename and vocabulary identify proper-name Paradox; a paradox changes it to a generic noun.
Stun Vindicta exactly matches the command filename and authoritative character spelling; Son/Sun are phonetic errors.
The component revisions are nonsensical and fail to express Wraith seeing Forge/McGinnis.
Seven is the authoritative character name; Seventh is a phonetic substitution.
Cover is more plausible ability terminology than Clover, but no repository ability vocabulary confirms Wrecker's spoken ability-one name.
I admit it and I mean it are both coherent but semantically different spoken openings.
Rich people and most people are distinct, grammatical subjects; the surrounding examples do not determine which was spoken.
Has proven, is proving, and this professor is proving are all grammatical but encode tense/article differences.
Neither waste nor wait my colleagues here about this forms a grammatical or coherent Dynamo upgrade line.
Both component revisions are ungrammatical; neither can express the apparent lost moment-of-glory complaint.
Repository lore repeatedly calls an individual OSIC operative a Sandman, and parallel Haze dialogue says I'm a Sandman; revision 2 is grammatical.
Maelstrom is established world terminology and Mystic Goods is the coherent shop phrase; masterroom is corrupt.
Grace and Ray may be phonetic or prototype personal names for Wraith, and the later Archmother official line is different era-specific dialogue.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Warden; Ward is incomplete.
Boon is the established term for a patron blessing and matches the grant-boon filename; boom is a phonetic error.
Neither Hay nor Kay identifies authoritative Haze in the Rejuvenator event.
Holliday's locked them down is grammatical present-perfect phrasing and matches the lasso event; lock them is malformed after Holliday's.
Both component revisions say guys and fail to identify Geist in the item-check ping.
Grill, Crails, and Crills all fail to preserve authoritative Krill in the garage ping.
We need and the elliptical Need differ by a spoken subject; both are natural training reminders.
Both options are contextually broken; the likely contrast would require Not with making, which neither existing revision contains.
They're taking our tier one is the complete objective-under-attack warning; out tier one is wrong, and words fit repository transcript style better than numeral 1.
Armor and arm do not match the idol/Spirit Urn objective indicated by the filename; neither is a defensible transcript.
Both component revisions garble authoritative Infernus and have broken direct-address punctuation.
The filename and authoritative character list require Lash; last is a phonetic error.
Gate/Game fail to identify Geist in the enemy-swap warning; neither component revision is correct.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Calico; Caligo is misspelled.
Assassinate is Vindicta's established ultimate/command name and forms the standard ability-on-cooldown callout.
Vindicta's ruthless select context supports Today isn't the day for mercy; the affirmative version reverses the intended meaning.
Crackers and Tracker do not identify the Rutger/Bracca target in the garage ping.
We've got and we got are distinct spoken dialect/contraction forms; both fit the payday line.
Mole people is the character-specific joke for Mo and Krill; Hole people is a phonetic error.
The line clearly refers to character Lash rather than lass, but the existing revision lowercases the proper title The Lash and is not exact enough to auto-apply.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Calico; Calo is truncated.
Both component sentences are unusual but grammatical enough to be possible; adding it is audible and unselectable from an unselect filename.
Neither revision identifies Dynamo or forms the expected on-top-of-garage ping.
Kate and Kade both fail to identify authoritative Cadence in the garage ping.
You're not a friend is grammatical; You're not a my friend contains incompatible articles.
A far-snipe reaction concerns how Vindicta hit the shot; hid does not fit the event.
Say the word and I can fly in is the coherent activation offer for Ivy's flying ability; fly it is semantically wrong.
Both Spanish revisions have incorrect interrogative/agreement for the apparent catch-me challenge; neither is clearly valid.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Haze; Hayes/he's are phonetic errors.
The filename and authoritative character vocabulary require Haze; he's/Hayes are phonetic errors.
Spirit Urn is the authoritative game-object term and matches the idol-drop bridge event; earn/earned are phonetic errors.
Both revisions are garbled and fail to identify historical Sandeep under the garage.
Both revisions garble the expected Check out what Seven bought item ping as seven bolt/bold.
The filename and authoritative character spelling require Lash; Lush is a phonetic error.
BOLT and Boat both fail to express the expected Check out what Calico bought item ping.
Oathkeeper is established throughout Lady Geist's story and independently confirmed by the official line; Hidden King wording remains separate.
Nashala is authoritative and the official line independently confirms the same sentence core; the Archmother-specific replacement remains separate.
The way people will love me is more coherent than the right people will love me, but the opening still sounds incomplete without recording context.
Rackets is the established term for dubious criminal services and supports Wraith's protection joke; erratic does not fit labeling services.
The official parallel lacks all and supports Such arcane mysteries I will show you, but the older recording may audibly include all.
Ugh and Oh are distinct audible interjections and cannot be inferred from upgrade context.
Burgeoning empire is the established phrase and yields a coherent Seven line; burdening and burning embargo are phonetic corruptions.
A museum and the museum are both grammatical and differ by a spoken article.
Capitalized Sitha is plausibly a fictional occult power in Geist's lore, while sigma reads as a phonetic/meme substitution; no vocabulary entry confirms Sitha.
Fortune's lover is a coherent sarcastic epithet for Holliday and preserves a possessive phrase; no repository term confirms it over Fortis lover.
